stories.title: Altman: OpenAI now writes explicit safety cases before frontier RL runs - and backs a federal frontier-safety framework
stories.summary: In a long thread, Altman says OpenAI writes explicit safety cases before frontier RL runs expected to jump capability - not just before release - and backs a federal frontier-safety framework with independent auditors, while insisting labs will not wait for legislation or an antitrust exemption. He names two failure modes the cases must address: loss of control, and concentration of power in one person/company/country. For builders this is the first concrete 'pacing is a process artifact, not a stop' claim from a frontier lab CEO, landing in the same week as Amodei's 12 Sep 'We Must Pace the Frontier' essay. Caveat: no spec, eval protocol, auditor names, or OpenAI blog attached - this is a CEO process claim, not a model or benchmark drop.

stories.title: Pre-cloture squeeze: banking groups demand tighter stablecoin rewards, bipartisan state AG coalition urges rejection, Lummis says Dems 'simply won't'
stories.summary: The eve of Tuesday's 60-vote cloture test on the Clarity Act ran on lobbying, not votes: eight US banking groups (ABA, BPI, ICBA among them) asked Senate leaders to tighten stablecoin-reward language that still permits interest-like payments; NY AG Letitia James is leading a bipartisan coalition of ~17-18 state AGs urging rejection over federal preemption via the 'qualified transaction' definition; and Bessent and Lummis traded cabinet-level endorsements vs. 'Democrats simply won't' quotes. Builders should read this as the bill's last substantive pressure points (rewards + state enforcement) before the procedural vote; none of it is law yet.

quality.note: In-window lobbying/quote cluster ahead of the 15 Sep cloture vote (covered as the final-text release yesterday). Letter and coalition are primary artifacts via outlet posts; AG count 17-18 per the CoinDesk article. Vote outcome not yet known.

stories.title: Catch-up: @foundmyfitness recaps the 117-year-old supercentenarian study - short telomeres + aged immune cells, but epigenetic age ~23 years younger
stories.summary: Patrick McKenzie (@foundmyfitness) posted (14 Sep 14:10 UTC) a recap of the most comprehensive supercentenarian study to date - the multi-omic analysis of Maria Branyas (117) from the Esteller group (Josep Carreras Institute, Cell Reports Medicine): exceptionally short telomeres and an aged pro-inflammatory immune system coexisting with a genuinely low-inflammation state, protective genetic variants, a bifidobacteria-dominated microbiome and an epigenetic age ~23 years below chronological. The underlying paper is from Sep 2025 - outside the window, hence Catch-up (canonical URL absent from this edition and archives) - but it is the definitive n=1 dataset on how extreme longevity actually looks biologically. Caveat: n=1, observational; her biology is not a formula, as the recap itself notes.

Caveat: it is a news report, not a peer-reviewed paper, and the tuned model is not public.

stories.title: Science Translational Medicine: slow-wave-synchronized auditory stimulation increases CSF flow in humans - a lever on glymphatic clearance
stories.summary: An STM paper (amplified by @ScienceMagazine 14 Sep 18:00 UTC) reports that closed-loop auditory pink-noise stimulation timed to EEG slow-wave peaks increased cerebrospinal fluid flow in healthy adults napping inside an MRI (n=14). For builders this is a rare human proof-of-concept on the glymphatic-clearance question: if you can pharmacologically or behaviorally deepen slow-wave coupling, you may modulate the brain's waste-transport system implicated in neurodegenerative disease. It is a healthy-volunteer proof of concept - not a patient trial, not an aging intervention, and the dose-response and durability are unknown.

stories.title: Insilico's rentosertib: phase 2a participants show 3-4 year reversal in predicted biological age on six proteomic clocks
stories.summary: Medical News Today's 13 Sep report on the Insilico Medicine rentosertib phase 2a trial (the AI-designed drug for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) says participants experienced reversal of predicted biological aging across six proteomic clock models, with the peak effect at week 4 of about 3-4 years of biological-age reversal. For builders this is the first time a drug-candidate trial has reported a multi-clock proteomic reversal at this magnitude - and the 9 Sep Nature Methods paper (covered 09-08) had already published the integrated-clock methodology, so the measurement layer and the result layer now line up. It is human clinical data, but a small phase 2a with aging as an exploratory endpoint - not a geroprotective indication - and the clocks are predictive models, not ground truth.

stories.title: Reward AI exits stealth with OM-1 - a robot manipulation policy trained only on human demo data, zero-shot across embodiments
stories.summary: Stealth startup Reward AI debuted OM-1, a foundational manipulation policy trained entirely on direct human manipulation data - no teleoperation, no on-robot experience - built on the Omnibody Hand, a wearable 7-DoF mocap device derived from Stanford's DexCap research (tactile feedback, proximity sensing, global-shutter in-hand cameras, electromagnetic tracking). For builders this is the strongest in-window argument for the 'human-data-first' school against web-scale video pretraining (Dyna-2-style) and fleet teleoperation (Skild S1-style) - all claims are company-reported, no paper yet.
